extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: CT-RATE is a public dataset that pairs 3D medical images with corresponding textual reports. It comprises 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices). Each scan is accompanied by its corresponding radiology report including impression and findings sections. Each volume is also annotated with 18 abnormalities. The dataset is used to develop CT-CLIP (a CT-focused contrastive language-image pretraining framework) and CT-CHAT (a vision-language foundational chat model for 3D chest CT volumes).
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Bjoern Menze, and collaborators from University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Istanbul Medipol University, Boston University, NIH, Imperial College London, University Hospital Zurich, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg
extraction.publisher: Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital / University of Zurich
extraction.citeAs: Hamamci, I.E., Er, S., Wang, C., et al. Developing generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography. arXiv:2403.17834v4 [cs.CV] 30 Sep 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE was curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. It consists of non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. Each CT exam is accompanied by a radiology report authored by a radiologist, including impression and findings sections. The dataset captures substantial heterogeneity in CT scanners, acquisition protocols, and reconstruction techniques. All patient data was anonymized prior to computational analysis, with ethical approval granted by the Clinical Research Ethics Committee at Istanbul Medipol University.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Detailed metadata for the second external validation set (UPMC) is not publicly available, as it is a private dataset and cannot be shared. The RAD-ChestCT external validation set lacks a Mosaic attenuation label and does not include paired radiology reports.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. CT volumes are provided in various resolutions (512×512, 768×768, 1024×1024 px). Radiology reports are structured into four sections: clinical information, technique, findings, and impression. Reports were originally in Turkish and translated to English.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Reports were anonymized by removing all personal information using regular expressions to identify and eliminate date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. Anonymized reports were translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API. Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations and removed any residual personal information. CT volumes were anonymized by removing all identifying information from metadata. Volumes involving contrast material or body parts other than the chest were excluded. Each chest CT volume's orientation was standardized by examining its metadata.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each CT volume was resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. CT volumes were then either center-cropped or padded to reach a consistent resolution of 480×480×240. Each CT volume was converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from the metadata. HU values were clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000. During training, values were normalized to a range of -1 to 1. For the CT-Net baseline, chest CT volumes were resized to 420×420×402. The dataset was divided into training (20,000 patients) and internal validation (1,304 patients) sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-abnormality labels were extracted from radiology reports using an automated text classifier. 1,000 reports were manually annotated for 18 distinct abnormalities by merging findings and impression sections. Conditions not referenced in either section were considered absent. Similar conditions were grouped (e.g., left and right mucoid impactions under mucoid impaction; lung opacity, density increase, and ground-glass opacities under lung opacity; lung and fissural nodules as lung nodules). The annotated reports were divided into training (80%, 800 reports) and validation (20%, 200 reports) sets. A pretrained language model, RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, was finetuned on these annotations and then applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports. For expert evaluation of CT-CHAT report generation, three board-certified radiologists (two thoracic radiologists from Zurich and one from Istanbul) independently rated 150 reports per model on a 0-10 scale against predefined criteria covering finding description, localisation, terminology, and overall clinical adequacy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned text encoder's performance was evaluated using precision, recall, and F1 scores for each of the 18 abnormalities, showing robust classification (F1 scores ranging from 0.95 to 1.00 across abnormalities). For the expert radiologist evaluation, cases were stratified by Llama score into low (0-3), medium (4-6), and high (7-10) clinical accuracy ranges, with 50 cases selected from each range to ensure balanced difficulty. Reports were presented anonymized to readers.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each report is annotated with 18 binary abnormality labels. For the expert evaluation, each of 150 selected reports was rated by 3 board-certified radiologists.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected Turkish-to-English translations of radiology reports. Three board-certified radiologists (two thoracic radiologists from University Hospital Zurich and one from Istanbul Medipol University) performed expert evaluation of generated reports.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (finetuned for automated label extraction from radiology reports); Google Translate API (for Turkish-to-English translation of reports); TotalSegmentator (for organ-level anatomical segmentation labels); Llama 3.1 8B (for generating VQA question-answer pairs); Llama 3.1 70B (for clinical accuracy scoring of model outputs).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The CT-RATE dataset is publicly accessible via HuggingFace (https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibrahimhamamci/CT-RATE). The authors plan to extend CT-RATE with multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels for 3D chest CT volumes as future work. Organ-level anatomical segmentation labels are already openly available through the CT-RATE repository on Hugging Face. Trained models and codebase are publicly available at https://github.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CLIP and https://github.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CHAT.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient age (ranging from 18 to 102 years, mean 48.8 years), sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male), and medical history (symptoms described in clinical information section of reports). All personal information was anonymized prior to release: patient and medical professional identifiers were removed from reports and metadata.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: CT-RATE addresses critical challenges in 3D medical imaging by providing the first large-scale open-source dataset pairing 3D chest CT volumes with radiology reports. This enables development of AI foundation models that can assist radiologists in diagnosing various abnormalities, potentially reducing workload on radiologists and improving patient care. The dataset and associated models could be particularly valuable in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available. The open-source release lays the groundwork for future innovations in medical AI.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: CT-RATE is a single-institution dataset from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital in Türkiye, which may introduce geographic and clinical setting biases that limit generalizability to other populations. The data originates from a single geographic and clinical setting. CT-CLIP depends on the specific terminology used in reports, and variability in how diseases are described across radiology reports can affect detection accuracy. Performance increases with larger training sets, suggesting that incorporating data from multiple institutions and more diverse patient populations could further enhance model robustness.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is from a single institution, which may limit generalizability to other populations and clinical settings. Current models are limited to chest CT volumes and do not cover other 3D imaging modalities (MRI, PET) or other anatomical regions. The absence of true 3D benchmarks for multimodal AI assistants limits comparative evaluation. CT-CHAT's report generation quality remains insufficient for clinical deployment. The dataset does not yet include multi-abnormality segmentation and localization labels (planned for future work). Detailed metadata for the UPMC external validation set is not publicly available.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and fine-tuning of AI models for: (1) multi-abnormality detection in 3D chest CT volumes (18 abnormalities); (2) CT volume-to-volume retrieval; (3) report-to-volume retrieval; (4) radiology report generation; (5) visual question answering for 3D chest CT; (6) contrastive language-image pretraining for 3D medical imaging. The dataset supports both self-supervised and supervised learning approaches. Not recommended for clinical deployment without further validation, as model performance does not yet meet clinical deployment thresholds.
